pm_exper_user_2079_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I stay calm and focused when participating in a live, globally broadcast panel discussion with influential world leaders?
pm_exper_user_2079_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Given your past anxiety before addressing the UN General Assembly, it may help to reframe the broadcast as an extension of your day-to-day advocacy, focusing on the evidence and stories you’ve prepared rather than the audience size. Ground yourself with a few slow, deliberate breaths just before speaking to anchor your focus.
(b) Since you’ve previously experienced stress in high-profile UN speaking roles, you might benefit from rehearsing your core points aloud in a simulation setting with trusted colleagues. This can help recreate the pressure in a controlled way, allowing you to enter the panel with familiar mental and physical cues.
(c) For high-stakes panel discussions, it often helps to view the conversation as an opportunity to share valuable insights rather than as a personal performance. A brief grounding exercise, like deep breathing or focused visualization, can help you stay present and collected when the broadcast begins.
(d) Recalling that live addresses in the UN context have triggered anxiety for you before, consider developing a short pre-panel ritual—such as reviewing a meaningful photograph from your field work—to shift your attention to the humanity behind your words rather than the scale of the stage.
